name: balanced-engine
message: Engine balance: multiplicative difficulty for batting and bowling, ball quality fights back, defensive shots, bowler quality follows rating (switch BALANCED_ENGINE)

ops.find:
/**
     * Master switch for the bowling-balance fix (set to false to get the old behaviour back exactly).
     *
     * Why it exists: measured on a twin of this engine (tools/difficulty_twin.js), a T20 innings against
     * the USER'S bowling gave the computer side ~245 runs for ~3.4 wickets on Medium, ~1.9 wickets on
     * Hard and ~1 on Hardest. Three loopholes did that:
     *  1. Difficulty was ADDED to the wicket chance (0.05 - 0.06 on Hardest = below zero, i.e. floored
     *     at 0.1% a ball): on Hard/Hardest wickets almost stopped existing.
     *  2. The computer batter saw the real length and the real quality of every ball before choosing
     *     footwork and shot, and nearly always picked a shot rated "Excellent" for it (wicket chance x0.22,
     *     boundaries x1.9). A real batter misreads some deliveries.
     *  3. The batting side's multipliers (footwork 0.7 x shot 0.22 x timing 0.4 = 0.06) outweigh the
     *     bowling side's best (about 2.4), so even a perfect ball was usually safe.
     * Only the computer batter against the user's bowling changes; the user's batting, the computer's
     * bowling and computer-v-computer matches (AiBallModel) are untouched.
     */
    const val BALANCED_USER_BOWLING = true

    /** The computer batter is not a perfect batter: his wickets are more likely, his boundaries fewer. */
    private const val AI_BATTER_WICKET_FACTOR = 1.9
    private const val AI_BATTER_BOUNDARY_FACTOR = 0.6
ops.replace:
/**
     * Master switch for the engine-balance fixes (false = the original rules, exactly).
     * Measurements: DIFFICULTY_NOTES.md and tools/difficulty_twin.js (a twin of this engine; run it with node).
     *
     * Before, in a T20 the computer batters made ~234 runs for ~3.5 wickets even against computer bowlers of
     * their own level, and the user's difficulty setting made it worse. What this changes, for the user
     * AND the computer alike:
     *  1. Difficulty is multiplicative. It used to be ADDED, which on Hard/Hardest pushed the wicket chance
     *     (user bowling) or the boundary chances (user batting) below zero, where they were floored at 0.1%:
     *     no wickets for the bowler, no boundaries for the batter.
     *  2. A good delivery fights back (BattingSystem.applyBallContest): the better the ball, the more of the
     *     batting bonuses are cancelled. A perfect shot against a perfect ball used to be a boundary 41% of the
     *     time; now it is about 14%.
     *  3. Defensive shots almost never reach the boundary, and a plainly wrong shot is punished a little less.
     *  4. The computer bowler's quality follows his rating (a 78 used to bowl 40% bad or very bad balls, now
     *     about 20%); the computer batter misjudges some deliveries and mistimes some shots.
     * Computer-v-computer matches in a tournament use AiBallModel and are untouched.
     */
    const val BALANCED_ENGINE = true

    private fun difficultyWicketFactor(d: Difficulty): Double = when (d) {
        Difficulty.EASY -> 1.25
        Difficulty.MEDIUM -> 1.0
        Difficulty.HARD -> 0.8
        Difficulty.HARDEST -> 0.62
    }

    private fun difficultyBoundaryFactor(d: Difficulty): Double = when (d) {
        Difficulty.EASY -> 0.9
        Difficulty.MEDIUM -> 1.0
        Difficulty.HARD -> 1.12
        Difficulty.HARDEST -> 1.25
    }

// 17 before the balanced engine; 12 now (a wrong shot is still the worst thing a batter can do).
                multiplyKey(probs, OutcomeProbs::wicket, if (MatchEngine.BALANCED_ENGINE) 12.0 else 17.0)

ops.content:
# Difficulty and engine balance

Switch: `MatchEngine.BALANCED_ENGINE` (true = balanced, false = the original rules exactly).
Measure it yourself: `node tools/difficulty_twin.js` (a twin of `MatchEngine.simulateBall`, no network needed).

## What players saw
Computer bowlers got no wickets, computer batters hit boundaries off perfect balls, defensive shots sometimes went
for four, 75 to 80 rated bowlers bowled many bad balls, and on Hard / Hardest the user could not score.
All of it is real, and measured (T20, balanced pitch):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Perfect shot v perfect ball | 29% four, 12% six (2.4 runs a ball) | 10% four, 4.5% six (1.4 runs a ball) |
| Good shot v perfect ball | 10% four, 4% six | 6% four, 3% six |
| Forward defence (perfect timing) | four about 1 ball in 140 | about 1 in 500 |
| Computer bowler rated 80, bad + very bad balls | 38% | 18% |
| Computer bowler rated 90 | 34% | 10% |
| Computer v computer, equal skill | 234 runs, 3.5 wickets | 166 runs, 6.8 wickets |

User batting, runs / wickets lost (skilled | average player):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Easy | 217 / 2.5 \| 160 / 4.1 | 154 / 6.1 \| 106 / 8.4 |
| Medium | 187 / 4.8 \| 129 / 7.7 | 143 / 7.2 \| 94 / 9.1 |
| Hard | 139 / 6.9 \| 86 / 9.3 | 132 / 8.1 \| 81 / 9.6 |
| Hardest | 79 / 8.5 \| 49 / 9.9 | 114 / 9.0 \| 67 / 9.9 |

User bowling, runs conceded / wickets taken (skilled | average player):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Easy | 161 / 5.8 \| 177 / 5.5 | 155 / 7.7 \| 183 / 6.9 |
| Medium | 215 / 3.9 \| 239 / 3.6 | 168 / 6.7 \| 198 / 5.9 |
| Hard | 252 / 2.0 \| 278 / 1.9 | 182 / 5.6 \| 211 / 4.9 |
| Hardest | 276 / 1.0 \| 304 / 0.9 | 194 / 4.5 \| 223 / 4.0 |

"Skilled" and "average" are models of how well a human reads the ball, times it and lands his deliveries; real players
will differ. Field placement is not modelled, so the real game gets slightly more wickets than the table says.

## The loopholes (all fixed unless marked)
1. Difficulty was ADDED to the probabilities. On Hardest the wicket chance (user bowling) or the four and six chances
   (user batting) went below zero and were floored at 0.1%. Now difficulty is multiplicative, the same factor on both
   sides inverted: wickets x1.25 / 1.0 / 0.8 / 0.62 and boundaries x0.9 / 1.0 / 1.12 / 1.25 for the bowler's side.
2. The batting layers (footwork, shot fit, intent, timing) multiplied the wicket chance down to a few percent and
   boundaries up 3 to 4 times, and nothing depended on how good the ball was. Now the ball fights back
   (`BattingSystem.applyBallContest`); `CONTEST_STRENGTH` makes it stricter or weaker.
3. Defensive shots: boundaries cut to about a quarter of what they were. A wrong shot's wicket multiplier 17 -> 12.
4. Computer bowler quality ignored his rating (25 + rating x 0.45, flat +/-48 spread). Now 13 + rating x 0.70 with a
   triangular spread, so a 78 bowls about 20% bad or very bad balls, not 40%.
5. Computer batter: saw the real length and quality of every ball (now misjudges 20 to 45% of lengths) and his timing
   luck was a flat spread (now triangular around a slightly lower base).
6. Not changed: only the exact centre of a length band scores a perfect delivery for the USER, so Perfect is a narrow
   target for a human bowler; a Good delivery gives no bonus. Say if you want it widened.
7. Not changed: after two early wickets the computer batters defend heavily (`AiSituation.battingBias`), which keeps
   wickets from falling in clusters.

## Where to turn the dials
`MatchEngine.difficultyWicketFactor` / `difficultyBoundaryFactor`, `BattingSystem.CONTEST_STRENGTH`, the `0.70` in
`BowlingSystem.generateAiBowlingDecision`, and the misread chance and timing base in `generateAiBattingDecision`.
